title: customer-sandbox-hybrid-egress-and-dns-handoff-workshop-notes
content:
Context and goals:
- Customer: retail-analytics startup running sensitive user profiles in a sandbox VPC (dev/staging) and planning a private inference POC in our Private offering.
- Goal: land a safe, testable hybrid egress + DNS handoff design for the POC that preserves data isolation, allows controlled external model pulls (container images/models), and provides predictable observability for SRE and SE teams.
- Constraints: no internet-facing load balancers in sandbox; vendor image pulls must be allowed only to a short whitelist; minimal changes to customer's existing DNS zone; low-touch for customer ops.

Workshop agenda (90m):
1) 10m - Introductions and constraints recap (security, compliance, test data)
2) 20m - Current sandbox topology walkthrough (customer network owner)
3) 30m - Proposed hybrid egress patterns and DNS handoff options (this doc)
4) 20m - Quick decision matrix and action items + owner assignment
5) 10m - Live checklist and follow-ups

Topology summary (from customer):
- Single sandbox VPC per environment (dev/stage), CIDR 10.10.0.0/16, /24 subnets across 3 AZs.
- Transit connectivity to corp via Transit Gateway (TGW) exists but restricted.
- CI runners in the same VPC; need to fetch model artifacts from vendor s3-like endpoints.
- No NAT currently; instances have no public IPs.
- Route53 private zone for corp.internal (split-horizon used by prod).

Design options considered (high level):
A) Local NAT gateway per sandbox VPC + Route53 forwarding rules
  - pros: simple, minimal infra changes.
  - cons: broad egress footprint; lacks per-service auditability; cost scales with data egress.

B) Centralized egress proxy (managed EC2/Autoscaling group or EKS sidecar) behind TGW with allowlist and per-tenant headers
  - pros: request-level observability, fine-grained allowlist, uniform TLS termination and mTLS to downstream vendors possible.
  - cons: introduces single host/ASG to manage; slightly higher latency; needs HA design.

C) AWS PrivateLink / Interface VPC Endpoints to vendor-managed connectors + Route53 Resolver outbound endpoints
  - pros: very tight security (no internet egress), predictable connectivity to partner endpoints; highly auditable.
  - cons: requires vendor support for PrivateLink; potentially expensive for multiple partners.

D) Egress-only IG + TLS-forwarding proxy in restricted subnet with NACL + SG layering
  - pros: inexpensive; simpler than centralized proxy with full L7 inspection.
  - cons: coarse control; harder to add header-level routing or per-tenant tagging.

Decision matrix (quick scoring from workshop):
- Security: C > B > D > A
- Operational effort: A > D > B > C (A easiest)
- Observability & audit: B > C > D > A
- Cost: A < D < B < C (A cheapest)

Workshop recommendation (consensus):
- Short-term (POC): implement a hybrid of A + B: a small local NAT for emergency/CI pulls plus a lightweight centralized egress proxy (managed ASG with healthchecks) for inference traffic. Route inference traffic through the proxy via explicit SG rules and iptables-based mark+route on the inference hosts.
- Long-term (post-POC): evaluate PrivateLink with the vendor for production if vendor supports it; otherwise keep centralized proxy with per-tenant mTLS and mutual auth.

Concrete POC design (details):
1) Network layout
   - Keep existing sandbox VPC (10.10.0.0/16).
   - Create a dedicated 'egress-subnet' (10.10.254.0/28) with 2 AZ-backed instances (proxy-asg) in that subnet.
   - Retain a single small NAT gateway in one AZ as fallback for CI jobs (tagged "ci-nat-fallback").

2) Proxy design
   - Service: HA HTTP(s) forward proxy (squid / Envoy) running in ASG behind internal NLB.
   - Ports: 3128 (HTTP proxy), 8443 (HTTPs-forwarding), 15001 (admin).
   - Auth: client certs (mTLS) and IP allowlist.
   - Logging: structured access logs to an S3 bucket + CloudWatch LogGroup with lifecycle 90d.

3) DNS handoff
   - Use Route53 Resolver outbound endpoints in sandbox VPC to forward to a resolver in the egress VPC (or the customer's corp resolver) for vendor hostnames requiring split-horizon.
   - For public vendor domains used only by inference, create private Route53 zones in the sandbox and populate A/AAAA records pointing to the PrivateLink endpoints (future) or to the proxy IPs (during POC).
   - TTL guidance: set low TTL (60s) during POC to iterate quickly; increase to 300s or 900s in production.

4) Routing strategy
   - Use iptables MARK + ip rule to mark inference process traffic (uid or cgroup) and route-mark to the proxy's ENI IP as next-hop.
   - Example (linux host):
     - iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -m owner --uid-owner inference -j MARK --set-mark 0x1
     - ip rule add fwmark 0x1 table 200
     - ip route add default via 10.10.254.5 dev eth1 table 200
   - This keeps non-inference traffic using default VPC routes/NAT.

5) Security controls
   - SGs: only allow inference hosts to speak to proxy's SG on 3128/8443. Proxy SG only allows outbound to vendor IPs/ports on 443.
   - NACLs: keep permissive for subnets but rely on SGs for enforcement.
   - IAM: proxy EC2 instance profile limited to log s3 write and CloudWatch put.
   - KMS: Use a dedicated KMS key for proxy TLS certs if storing secrets.

6) Observability & tests
   - Synthetic test plan: 1) curl vendor model metadata endpoint (both A and via proxy), 2) small model pull (10MB) to validate NAT vs proxy path, 3) latency microbenchmarks (p50/p95 for metadata, model chunk pulls).
   - Metrics: per-request latency, TLS handshake time, bytes egressed, error rates, per-tenant RPM.
   - Add tracing headers (x-request-id, x-tenant-id) at the proxy and carry them to logs.

7) Failover and graceful degradation
   - Healthcheck: ALB/NLB target health using /healthz that checks upstream vendor reachability on a minimal GET.
   - On proxy outage: route table fallback via ip rule removed and traffic flows to NAT fallback for non-model large pulls. For inference-critical calls, fail closed (reject) unless specifically allowed.

8) Quick terraform snippets (POC - textual reference only)
   - resource "aws_instance" "proxy" {
       ami = "ami-xxxx"
       instance_type = "t3.medium"
       subnet_id = aws_subnet.egress_subnet.id
       tags = { Name = "sandbox-egress-proxy" }
     }

   - route53-resolver rule sample (forward):
     - aws_route53_resolver_rule: domain_name = "vendor.example.com"; rule_type = "FORWARD"; resolver_endpoint_id = "rslv-out-abc"; target_ip: 10.1.2.3

Open questions / risks captured in workshop:
- Vendor support for PrivateLink unknown (action: SE to confirm with vendor - JIRA-7891).
- Per-tenant bandwidth throttling: we need a quota mechanism on the proxy (Envoy rate limiting or token bucket). (owner: Ravi)
- Cost: NAT vs PrivateLink cost estimation for expected model pulls (owner: Finance contact).
- TLS termination vs passthrough: which vendors require SNI passthrough? If passthrough needed, we cannot do header injection. (owner: Priya)
- DNS complexity: customer uses an on-prem resolver for some vendor domains; Route53 Resolver forwarding may need cross-account permissions.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- SE: spin up proxy ASG PoC in customer sandbox (task: JIRA-7902) - owner: Ava.
- Customer network owner: provide up-to-date list of outbound vendors and IP ranges (due: 2024-09-10) - owner: Maria (customer).
- SE: run synthetic model pull tests and upload csv of p50/p95 latencies to Confluence (JIRA-7903) - owner: Ravi.
- SE: confirm vendor PrivateLink availability and pricing (owner: Priya).
- Security review: provide short risk memo on allowing NAT fallback and expected audit logs (owner: Security team contact).

Notes-to-self / workshop leftovers:
- Keep the iptables mark implementation as the default — it's least invasive to application code (no code change needed if inference runs as a specific uid).
- Consider cgroups v2 network namespace approach if we need per-process net isolation later.
- If central proxy becomes production, design for instance replacement without IP change (use ENI with static private IP or internal NLB).

Appendix: quick smoke test commands (for SE runbook)
1) Verify proxy reachability: curl -v --proxy http://10.10.254.5:3128 https://vendor.example.com/healthz
2) Verify marked routing: iptables -t mangle -L OUTPUT -n; ip rule show; ip route show table 200
3) Validate DNS forwarding: dig @10.10.0.2 vendor.example.com +short; dig vendor.example.com (should resolve to PrivateLink IP or to proxy).

End of notes — captured live during 2024-09-03 workshop.
